en: Using an inclined plane like a wooden ramp reduces the lifting force needed to move heavy boxes, preventing back injuries.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with wet floors, which prevents dangerous slips and falls during the rainy season.
Gravity pulls falling objects downward, so wearing a certified helmet protects your skull from impact injuries while riding a bicycle.
Keeping strong magnets away from magnetic stripe cards prevents the magnetic field from erasing the stored data and ruining the card.
Never touching electrical switches with wet hands prevents severe electric shocks because water is an excellent conductor of electricity.
Looking directly at a solar eclipse without certified eclipse glasses can permanently burn your retina due to intense invisible radiation.
Wearing foam earplugs at loud concerts protects your delicate eardrums from permanent damage caused by high-decibel sound waves.
Using thick cloth oven mitts prevents hand burns because the trapped air in the fabric acts as a thermal insulator.
Eating carbohydrates provides your body with chemical energy, which your digestive system converts into mechanical energy for muscle movement.
Using a wheelbarrow as a second-class lever multiplies your lifting force, allowing you to move heavy garden soil with less effort.
Applying lubricating oil to a rusty bicycle chain reduces harmful friction, making pedaling easier and preventing the metal from snapping.
Unplugging appliances by pulling the hard plastic plug prevents the internal copper wires from fraying and causing dangerous electric shocks.
